plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce single-name concentration.
This plan aims to significantly de-risk the portfolio by eliminating high-beta and leveraged positions.
It prioritizes capital preservation and stability over aggressive growth.
conservative.read: This conservative approach targets a modest ~1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. Expect significantly reduced volatility and drawdown risk. Returns will be lower, but the portfolio is better insulated from market downturns.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to reduce overall leverage and concentration.
Buy TECS at 4% as a new position, based on its strong scanner setup.
This strategy balances growth potential with risk management, maintaining a small leveraged component.

balanced.read: This balanced approach targets ~2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. Expect moderate volatility and drawdown potential. The blend of broad index, quality tech, and limited leverage aims for steady, sustainable growth.

plan: Add to existing leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to increase exposure.
Buy TECS at 6% as a new position, leveraging a strong scanner setup.
This plan aggressively leans into high-beta and leveraged positions for maximum growth potential.
Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage the amplified risks associated with this strategy.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth approach targets ~4% per month, stretching for higher returns. Be aware of significantly higher volatility, potential for larger drawdowns, and the daily decay/rebalancing effects of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is paramount to manage risk.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero.
